title: {{lena}} reads shared data from {{vocab.partnerShort}}
goal: {{lena}} works at {{vocab.partner}}. Their agent needs to read {{vocab.resource}} that we host, without a second account or a shared password.
obstacle: Two companies, two identity providers. We must take {{vocab.partnerShort}}'s word about who {{lena}} is, but only for what we choose to allow.
control: ID-JAG: the partner's IdP issues an Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant addressed to our authorization server, which redeems it for its own access token.
say: No shared passwords, no duplicate accounts, and we still decide what {{lena}}'s agent can read.

steps.title: Bring in the partner's ID-JAG
steps.tell: {{vocab.partnerShort}}'s IdP has already signed {{lena}} in and issued an ID-JAG for our authorization server. Here you paste it, or fetch one from xaa.dev's free IdP.
steps.say: The partner vouches for {{lena}}. We create no account for them.
steps.why: Identity travels from the company that actually knows the person.

steps.title: Check it against the draft
steps.tell: Before trusting it, the ID-JAG is checked against the IETF draft: type, issuer, a single audience, client_id, expiry.
steps.say: Every check has a name, so a refusal is never a mystery.
steps.why: Most partner-access failures are one wrong claim; this names it.

blocked.tell: Change one claim, a wrong audience for example, and the same check fails and names the claim.
blocked.say: One bad claim and the grant is refused, with the reason.

steps.title: Redeem it at our authorization server
steps.tell: Our authorization server verifies the partner's signature against the Trusted IdPs list and redeems the ID-JAG for its own access token, never granting more than the ID-JAG's scope.
steps.say: We trust {{vocab.partnerShort}} only because an admin approved it.
steps.why: Trust is an explicit, audited decision, not a side effect.

blocked.tell: If the partner's IdP is not on the Trusted IdPs list, or not yet approved, redemption is refused and the reason is recorded.
blocked.say: Unknown or unapproved IdP: no token.

steps.title: The agent calls {{vocab.resourceTool}}
steps.tell: {{lena}}'s agent calls {{vocab.resourceTool}} with the new access token. The server checks it against our authorization server's keys, so only what the token allows is listed.
steps.say: The agent sees only what its token says, nothing the partner can widen.
steps.why: The resource owner decides, not the partner.

blocked.tell: Call with no token, or with the raw ID-JAG: both are refused, and the server says which check failed.
blocked.say: The ID-JAG is not an access token, and the server knows the difference.

steps.title: Prove the refusals
steps.tell: Live negative tests break the assertion one way at a time and confirm the authorization server refuses each with an OAuth error and no token.
steps.say: We show the refusals, not just the happy path.
steps.why: A grant you cannot refuse is not a control.

proof.happy: The decoded access token: subject {{lena}}, scope limited to what was granted, issued by our authorization server.
proof.blocked: The refusal: an OAuth error that names the failed check, and no token.
